summary: The lecture covers the Aryan migration into northwestern India (c. 1500–600 BCE), the Vedic texts as primary sources, the Battle of Ten Kings involving Vishwamitra, and the four Vedas: Rigveda (10 mandalas), Samaveda (melodies), Yajurveda (sacrifices), and Atharvaveda (magic/philosophy).
points: Aryans (Indo-Aryans) migrated into northwestern India around 1500–600 BCE
Primary knowledge about Aryans comes from the Vedas, especially Rigveda
Battle of Ten Kings (Dasharajna) featured sage Vishwamitra
Rigveda is a collection of hymns divided into 10 mandalas
Samaveda is a collection of melodies (saman) for chanting
Yajurveda is a collection of sacrificial formulas (yajus)
Atharvaveda contains spells, charms, and philosophical hymns
Early Vedic society worshipped natural forces as gods (Indra, Agni, Varuna)
